commits.message:
[NVIDIA] Lower rounded float conversions with llvm.fptrunc.round (#12237)

Use `llvm.fptrunc.round` for NVIDIA `tt.fp_to_fp` narrowing between f16,
bf16, f32, and f64. This exposes rounding to LLVM and lets NVPTX fold
f16/bf16 conversions through an f32 intermediate into direct SM90+
instructions. It also covers scalar FP16 intermediates in the existing
FP8 conversion paths.

Includes the forward fix in #12407, which should merge first. The LLVM
pin update in #12236 has merged.

- Keep `arith::TruncFOp` on ordinary `llvm.fptrunc`.
- Accept `triton::RoundingMode` in `convertFpTrunc` and stringify it
internally.
- Preserve specialized packed FP8 conversions and migrate
conversion-instruction checks to `tritongpu_to_ptx.mlir`.
- Cover RTNE/RTZ narrowing, f16/bf16 conversions, and FP8 intermediates
in PTX tests for SM80, SM90, and SM100.

`18f9e623` build 2 SDK (archive checksum and configured SDK path
verified; LibLZMA discovery disabled):

rounding-boundary cases and exhaustive f16↔bf16 inputs in both
directions.

SM80/SM90 coverage above is compilation through PTX; GPU execution was

commits.message:
[AMD] Drop core LLVM workarounds after the LLVM bump (#12410)

Triton's core LLVM now includes llvm/llvm-project@5bf967cb132b and knows
the gfx1250-strict processor, so remove the workarounds that bridged the
gap to the independently pinned AMD code generator:

- Remove upgradeLegacyNamedBarriers from the codegen library. Core LLVM
already emits named barriers in address space 15, so restore the plain
parse path, which auto-upgrades debug info. Bump the AMD codegen build
number so the library is republished.
- Derive the amdgpu12.50s triple for gfx1250-strict from core LLVM. Drop
the hard-coded triple, the base-arch layout triple used around core LLVM
target machines, and the TRITON_DUMP_MIR/TRITON_SWAP_MIR restriction for
gfx1250-strict.

Add gfx1250-strict coverage for the target triple, the architected-SGPR
check, and the MIR round trip.

commits.comment: TritonGPU RemoveLayoutConversions 的优化：hoistConvertOnTopOfExtOrBroadcast 原先只支持单个扩展/广播 op（遇到第二个就 return false），现改为收集所有扩展/广播 op 并累计其转换代价 newCvtCost，仅当总代价仍小于原始转换代价时才提升。实现上把原来单 op 处理改为循环，同时收集 (op, srcEncoding) 并用 IRMapping 重写 slice。潜在风险：多个 op 的重写顺序与 mapping 一致性需保证（当前逐 op clone 后 setInsertionPoint 在 op 前，依赖 IRMapping 精确映射），以及代价模型的正确性依赖 getConvertCost 对每个 operand(0) 的估计。测试覆盖了多次 ext 与多次 broadcast 的正反例，合理。

commits.message:
[LLVM] Update LLVM to 18f9e623 (#12236)

Update the consumed LLVM SDK to
[`18f9e623e4c8`](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/18f9e623e4c891ba31ff817c07197707ac9bc593),
build 2, which includes the NVPTX `llvm.fptrunc.round` implementation.
All eight checksums come from the successful [post-merge SDK
build](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/actions/runs/38491954898)
triggered by #12262; all eight published archives are available. Build 2
disables the optional LibLZMA dependency so Linux consumers configure
without liblzma development files.

The LLVM/MLIR update requires these compatibility changes:

- Select NVPTX's `shortptr` ABI and preserve `enable_fp_fusion` through
contraction flags.
- Pass the new `pzo` operand as `false` to NVVM FP32-to-FP16/BF16 and
packed FP4 conversion intrinsics, preserving signed zero.
- Use the typed `LLVM::UMulHOp`, the updated pass APIs, and the new
inline-assembly convergence argument.
- Place AMD named barriers in their dedicated address space, 15, and
update their compile-only tests.
- Parse and restore LLVM TableGen library options alongside `cl::opt`,
so MIR dump/reload honors codegen start/stop points and scheduler
settings.
- Serialize alias-scope domains in the format supported by the
independently pinned AMD code generator, preserving explicit
alias/noalias relationships. Drop only the newer implicit disjoint-scope
guarantee at that handoff.
- Preserve Triton's existing assembly syntax through MLIR's
legacy-properties setting and keep supported attribute-dictionary
builder deprecations as warnings.
- Refresh affected lit expectations for LLVM/MLIR assembly and PTX
printing.

Rebased onto `2122e24efc`. Preserve upstream's `disable_lsr` option
alongside the new LLVM ABI handling. Update the rebased barrier-printing
expectations and remove the obsolete `llc -fp-contract=off` argument.

Validation on Brix GB300 at `f8ee3411f9`, with the published Ubuntu
ARM64 build-2 SDK and `CMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_LibLZMA=TRUE`:

- Native rebuild after the full build including Proton; verified the SDK
archive checksum, configured SDK path, changed source hashes, Python
package path, and AMD code-generator revision (`6bc4aaf6641c-3`).
- AMD code-generation and scheduler pytest suites: 25 passed, 2 GPU-only
tests skipped. Reproduced the alias-domain failure before the fix; added
coverage for named/anonymous domains, optional descriptions, and both
disjoint flag values.
- `make test-lit`: 305 passed, 2 unsupported. The FP4 regression now
translates through LLVM IR to PTX on SM100a.
- `make test-cpp`: 312 passed.
- Compiler-only, LLVM-option/ABI, LSR, BF16 rounding, and multiply-high
pytest coverage: 89 passed.
- FP32-to-FP16/BF16 downcast tests: 4 passed.
- Direct FP4 packing test: 1 passed, covering ties, saturation, nibble
order, and signed zero.
- Full `triton_kernels/tests/test_mxfp.py`: 172 passed.
- Pre-commit checks passed.

Follow-up validation on Brix GB300 at `df95c2e67c`:

- 313 native tests and 305 lit tests passed (2 unsupported).
- 33 AMD code-generation/scheduler tests passed (2 GPU-only tests
skipped), including eight MIR round trips across gfx90a, gfx942, gfx950,
and gfx1250 with machine scheduling both enabled and disabled.
- 74 compiler-option and compile-only tests passed.
- The CDNA5 compile-only suite passed at `8b935844c4`: 994 passed, 113
skipped.

[Full
CI](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/actions/runs/38986951213)
passed all 11 jobs at `df95c2e67c`: AMD gfx90a, gfx942, gfx950 (both
ROCm configurations), gfx1250 emulation, NVIDIA A100/H100/GB200, macOS,
formatting, and runner preparation. The NVIDIA conversion pattern is

commits.message:
[Testing] Create perf_report save_path before saving results (#12361)

Fixes #12359

`Mark._run` saves `<plot_name>.png` and `.csv` into `save_path`, but
`Mark.run` only created the directory in its `finally` block, after
`_run` had already failed. A first run with a new directory raised
`FileNotFoundError`, and the `finally` then created the directory, so a
second run passed.

Create `save_path` before running the benchmarks, and remove the
`makedirs` in `finally` since it is no longer needed.

Added `test_perf_report_creates_save_path` in
`python/test/unit/test_utils.py`. It fails without the fix
(`FileNotFoundError` on the png) and passes with it.

Verified on a Linux node (A40, no GPU needed for this path) by running
the new test with this checkout's `testing.py` over an installed triton
3.5.0, since the checkout is not built here. Ruff and yapf 0.43.0 are
clean. I did not run a full build or the rest of the unit suite.

Thanks to @zh301 for the report and reproducer.

commits.message:
[Gluon] Predicate TMEM copies and fix tutorial synchronization (#12402)

ConSan reports races in two Gluon tutorials: skipped pipeline iterations
in the block-scaled MMA tutorial still copy scales without waiting for
their load barrier, and im2col overwrites its single-buffered inputs
before the previous asynchronous MMA finishes reading them.

Add an optional predicate to `ttng.tmem_copy` and expose it as
`tcgen05_copy(..., pred=True)`. Carry the predicate through NVIDIA
lowering, compiler-generated MMA scale copies, ConSan, and FPSan.
Predicate the tutorial's scale copies and move im2col's MMA wait before
the next TMA loads.

Extend the existing lowering and GPU tests to cover dynamic true/false
predicates, destination preservation, subviews, and sanitizer behavior.

Validation:
- Rebuilt Triton on GB300 and verified that Python and native bindings
came from the tested checkout.
- Both complete tutorial pytest suites under ConSan: **433 passed, 64
skipped**, **9m24s wall time**.
- TMEM copy and ConSan/FPSan regression tests on GB300: **57 passed**.
- `make test-lit`: **305 passed, 2 unsupported**.
- All pre-commit hooks passed.

commits.comment: ConSan 分配 poison 初始化跨 CTA 同步修复：在 numCTAs>1 时用 hooks.createInitClusterBarrier 代替 CTA 局部 barrier，保证对 peer CTA 分配的首次访问前 poison 已完成；把 shared 的 async-proxy fence 移入 initializeAllocation 并在 barrier 之后发出（多 CTA 用 shared::cluster），TMEM 仍走 tmem store wait。同时移除测试里的手工 cluster barrier workaround。实现上把 hooks 与 hasAsyncProxyFenceTracking 传入 initializeAllocation，逻辑清晰；风险是 multi-CTA 下增加一次 cluster barrier 会有轻微性能开销，以及对单 CTA/多 CTA 分支需完整覆盖（已新增 2/4 CTA、multibuffer、单 CTA、关闭初始化及 NVIDIA/AMD shared 的 lit 期望）。

commits.message:
[ConSan] Synchronize allocation poisoning across CTAs (#11908)

ConSan's poison writes can race with a peer CTA's first access to an
allocation. In particular, a two-CTA MMA can access the peer's TMEM
before that CTA finishes poisoning it, corrupting the result with NaNs.

- Conservatively synchronize all CTAs after allocation poisoning
whenever `numCTAs > 1`, covering both TMEM initialization and
shared-memory initialization. Retain the CTA barrier for single-CTA
kernels.
- Remove the explicit cluster-barrier workaround from
`test_local_indexed_cross_cta_visibility` in
`python/test/gluon/test_consan.py`.
- Move the shared-memory async-proxy fence into `initializeAllocation`.
Emit it after the barrier, using `shared::cluster` coverage for
multi-CTA kernels and `shared::cta` for single-CTA kernels. This orders
the acquired poison stores, including peers' stores, before subsequent
async accesses. TMEM initialization continues to use its store wait.

Add lit coverage for two- and four-CTA TMEM initialization, multibuffer
allocations, single-CTA and disabled-initialization behavior, and
shared-memory initialization on NVIDIA and AMD. Check the proxy fence's
coverage and placement for single-CTA TMA, multicast TMA, and CLC.

Validation: compiler rebuild and both ConSan lit files passed; targeted
GPU tests passed with 99 passed and 20 skipped; `pre-commit run
--from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` passed.

commits.comment: 前端 hint 保真修复：新增单结果恒等 op tt.annotate（含 fold 与 canonicalizer：无属性时折叠、单结果 producer 时把属性下推后折叠），用于把 tt.call 上的 hint 精确附着到某个结果；TritonInlinerInterface::handleResult 对单结果 call 且存在 hint 时创建 AnnotateOp，AxisInfo 通过 IdentityOpAxisInfoVisitor 穿透，TritonToTritonGPU 用 GenericOpPattern，LLVM lowering 中 AnnotateOpConversion 直接替换。python/src/ir.cc 的 set_attr 对多结果 definingOp 自动插入 annotate 并重定向 uses。这是 TTIR 核心 IR 变更，影响所有后端，需注意 IR 兼容性与新增 op 在所有 pass 中的处理（已加 fold/canonicalize/lowering/axis）。

commits.message:
[FRONTEND] Preserve per-result hints through inlining (#12388)

Fixes #12366, Closes #12377

Compiler hints attached to a multi-result `tt.call` currently belong to
the shared operation, so inlining can propagate a hint to the wrong
returned value.

Add a single-result `tt.annotate` identity op and emit it only when
attaching a hint to a value from a multi-result operation. Fold
annotations into single-result producers, retain them for block
arguments and multi-result producers, propagate axis information through
them, and erase them during LLVM lowering. Single-result call hints are
also preserved when inlining returns an argument or a result of a
multi-result op.

Extend the existing inliner lit test for reordered, nested, duplicate,
mixed-rank, and split results. No runtime tests are added. This
addresses the issue described in #12377 while preserving the hints.

affected_interfaces: third_party/ascend/lib/TritonToLinalg/TritonToLinalgPass.cpp::TritonToLinalgPass::populateTritonToLinalgConversionPatterns (register a new conversion pattern for triton::AnnotateOp)
third_party/ascend/include/TritonToLinalg/TritonOpConverter.h::TTOpConverters (add AnnotateConverter identity pattern, modeled on BitcastConverter at line ~701)

third_party/ascend/lib/TritonToLinalg/TritonToLinalgPass.cpp::addDynamicLegal / convertRemainingComputations (triton::TritonDialect is illegal by default here, so an unhandled tt.annotate fails applyPartialConversion)

third_party/ascend/lib/TritonToStructured/PtrAnalysis.cpp::getDivisibility (reads tt.divisibility from value.getDefiningOp(); hints now live on a separate tt.annotate op for multi-result/block-arg values, so this analysis can miss them)
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: The commit adds a new `tt.annotate` identity op to the Triton dialect (TritonOps.td), emitted by the frontend via `Value::set_attr` (python/src/ir.cc) when a hint (tt.divisibility/tt.contiguity/tt.constancy from tl.multiple_of/tl.max_contiguous/tl.max_constancy) is attached to a value from a multi-result op, and by the inliner `handleResult` for single-result calls returning a block argument or multi-result producer. triton-ascend runs the upstream inliner + canonicalizer in `make_ttir` (third_party/ascend/backend/compiler.py), so the canonicalizer folds annotate into single-result producers but leaves annotate with block-argument or multi-result operands. Those survivors then reach TritonToLinalg, which has no pattern for `triton::AnnotateOp`, so `applyPartialConversion` fails with 'failed to legalize operation tt.annotate'. Adaptation: (1) add a trivial identity converter in TTOpConverters, e.g. `struct AnnotateConverter : public OpConversionPattern<triton::AnnotateOp> { matchAndRewrite -> rewriter.replaceOp(op, adaptor.getSrc()); return success(); }`, in third_party/ascend/include/TritonToLinalg/TritonOpConverter.h (mirror BitcastConverter); (2) register it in third_party/ascend/lib/TritonToLinalg/TritonToLinalgPass.cpp::populateTritonToLinalgConversionPatterns via `patterns.add<TTOpConverters::AnnotateConverter>(...)` (and confirm `triton::AnnotateOp` is illegal in addDynamicLegal so the pattern fires); (3) optionally update third_party/ascend/lib/TritonToStructured/PtrAnalysis.cpp::getDivisibility to look through a leading `triton::AnnotateOp` before reading `tt.divisibility`, otherwise the divisibility hint is lost for annotated values; (4) add a lit test under test/ exercising a kernel that annotates a tt.split/multi-result value.
deep_analysis.risk: Compilation-correctness regression, not a silent miscompile: without the conversion pattern, any kernel whose TTIR retains a `tt.annotate` op (e.g. tl.multiple_of applied to a tt.split/multi-result-call value, or an inlined single-result call returning a block argument) fails to compile with a 'failed to legalize operation' error. The adaptation itself is low-risk (pure identity erase of a side-effect-free op). Secondary, lower-severity risk: triton-ascend's PtrAnalysis reads `tt.divisibility` directly off the defining op, so if the pattern simply discards the hint instead of re-attaching it, divisibility-based pointer-alignment optimizations silently degrade for annotated values (no functional failure, just lost optimization).

[Gluon] Fix accumulator release and reject partial attention tiles (#12400)

Thanks to @vinodgro for reporting the issues.

Fix two errors in the Gluon Blackwell samples:

- In tutorial 08, advance the accumulator state only after releasing the
slot the epilogue read. Releasing the next slot can deadlock persistent
matmul when the MMA partition reaches its empty-buffer wait after the
epilogue's arrival.
- In the attention example, assert that the sequence length is divisible
by the effective `BLOCK_M` after CTA-layout scaling. Partial tiles can
make partitions disagree on the number of KV iterations and can write
across head boundaries or past the end of `M`.

Validated on GB300:
- 18 existing matmul test cases and 72 existing attention cases passed,
covering 1-, 2-, and 4-CTA attention configurations.
- With a uniform delay before the MMA partition's accumulator wait, the
original multi-tile matmul timed out after 60 seconds; the fixed version
passed three runs normally and three with ConSan, all checked against
the reference output. The original single-tile control passed.
- Ruff, YAPF, and whitespace checks passed.

commits.comment: 该 commit 解决的是 LLVM 通用 TTI 对 extractelement 过度计费导致 VectorCombine 将全元素使用的对齐向量 load 标量化、进而妨碍后续 NVPTX 打包向量化的问题。实现上新增 lib/Target/LLVMIR/LLVMIRNVPTXTargetInfo.cpp，定义派生自 TargetTransformInfoImplCRTPBase 的 TritonNVPTXTTIImpl（与 NoTTIImpl 同源），仅覆写三个 getVectorInstrCost 重载，使「固定向量 + 常量索引 + 32/64 位元素」的 extractelement 成本为 TCC_Free，其余查询（子字元素、动态索引等）沿用通用行为；未采用 BasicTTI/NVPTX target machine，以免牵连其他优化决策。LLVMPasses.h 暴露 createTritonNVPTXTargetIRAnalysis()，CMakeLists 增加编译单元。python/src/llvm.cc 的 optimize_module 新增 enable_nvptx_tti 参数（默认 false），并在注册 MAM/CGAM 分析之后、PassBuilder 安装默认 TargetIRAnalysis 之前通过 fam.registerPass 注册（首次注册生效）；条件为 !targetMachine 且 triple 为空或 NVPTX，从而不改变已有 target machine 的管线与其他后端。third_party/nvidia/backend/compiler.py 在 make_llir 中对 optimize_module 传 enable_nvptx_tti=True。测试上新增 test_bindings.py 中参数化用例，覆盖 7 种 dtype × 2/4 元素 × TTI 开关 × 三种 triple × 常量/动态索引，断言向量 load 是否被保留。风险较低：改动是新增可选能力且默认关闭，仅 NVIDIA 后端显式打开；但需注意 getVectorInstrCost 重载的签名与 LLVM 版本绑定，升级 LLVM 时需同步；此外 TTI 影响面广，若后续在此处增加更多 hook 需逐项验证。注意新参数为 optimize_module 的关键字参数，对既有调用（含 Ascend 的 optimize_module 调用）无破坏性。
commits.message:
[NVIDIA] Preserve unpacked vector loads with a conservative TTI (#12337)

LLVM's generic TTI charges for `extractelement` even when an element
already occupies a separate register. This can make VectorCombine
scalarize an aligned vector load whose elements are all used, obscuring
the vector structure needed by later optimizations.

Add a Triton NVPTX TTI derived from `TargetTransformInfoImplCRTPBase`,
the same generic foundation used by `NoTTIImpl`. Its first override
makes constant, in-range extracts from fixed vectors with 32- or 64-bit
elements free. Sub-word elements, dynamic indices, and other cost
queries retain the generic behavior. This provides a place to add
individually validated target information without adopting the full
NVPTX target-machine cost model.

The NVIDIA backend enables this analysis. Other backends and pipelines
with an explicit target machine keep their existing TTI. The binding
retains an opt-out for differential testing.

Two small synthetic loops illustrate the codegen effect. Each iteration
loads an aligned vector and adds each element to a separate loop-carried
FP32 accumulator. For example, the two-element loop starts with:

```llvm
%v = load <2 x float>, ptr addrspace(1) %p, align 8
%x0 = extractelement <2 x float> %v, i32 0
%x1 = extractelement <2 x float> %v, i32 1
%next0 = fadd float %sum0, %x0
%next1 = fadd float %sum1, %x1
```

With generic TTI, VectorCombine splits the load and the arithmetic stays
scalar. Preserving the vector load lets the existing NVPTX vectorizer
form packed accumulators. Compiling identical inputs with only
`enable_nvptx_tti` toggled (`O3`, SLP disabled, NVPTX vectorizer
enabled, `sm_100a`, PTX 9.4, ptxas 13.4.59) gives:

| Synthetic loop | Generic TTI: SASS per iteration | Custom TTI: SASS
per iteration | Registers, before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Two FP32 accumulators | 2 × `FADD` | 1 × `FADD2` | 8 → 8 |
| Four FP32 accumulators | 4 × `FADD` | 2 × `FADD2` | 14 → 14 |

For the two-element case, the PTX arithmetic changes from two
`add.rn.f32` instructions to one `add.rn.f32x2`. The actual SASS
arithmetic is:

```sass
// Before
FADD R5, R2, R5;
FADD R0, R3, R0;

// After: each operand denotes a pair of FP32 registers
FADD2 R2, R2.F32x2.HI_LO, R4.F32x2.HI_LO;
```

Both versions ultimately use one `LDG.E.64` (two elements) or one
`LDG.E.128` (four elements); the improvement here is packed arithmetic.
The same results hold when loading integer vectors and bitcasting them
to FP32. These are code-generation checks, not runtime speedup
measurements.

<details>
<summary>Standalone two-accumulator reproducer</summary>

Save this as `example.mlir`. This is a compiler-only example; its loop
executes at least once.

```mlir
module {
  llvm.func @accumulate(%input: !llvm.ptr<1>, %output: !llvm.ptr<1>, %count: i32) attributes {nvvm.kernel = 1 : ui1} {
    %c0 = llvm.mlir.constant(0 : i32) : i32
    %c1 = llvm.mlir.constant(1 : i32) : i32
    %c2 = llvm.mlir.constant(2 : i32) : i32
    %zero = llvm.mlir.constant(0.0 : f32) : f32
    llvm.br ^loop(%c0, %zero, %zero : i32, f32, f32)
  ^loop(%index: i32, %sum0: f32, %sum1: f32):
    %offset = llvm.mul %index, %c2 : i32
    %ptr = llvm.getelementptr %input[%offset] : (!llvm.ptr<1>, i32) -> !llvm.ptr<1>, f32
    %values = llvm.load %ptr {alignment = 8 : i64} : !llvm.ptr<1> -> vector<2xf32>
    %x0 = llvm.extractelement %values[%c0 : i32] : vector<2xf32>
    %next0 = llvm.fadd %sum0, %x0 : f32
    %x1 = llvm.extractelement %values[%c1 : i32] : vector<2xf32>
    %next1 = llvm.fadd %sum1, %x1 : f32
    %inc = llvm.add %index, %c1 : i32
    %more = llvm.icmp "ult" %inc, %count : i32
    llvm.cond_br %more, ^loop(%inc, %next0, %next1 : i32, f32, f32), ^exit {loop_annotation = #llvm.loop_annotation<unroll = <disable = true>>}
  ^exit:
    %out0 = llvm.getelementptr %output[%c0] : (!llvm.ptr<1>, i32) -> !llvm.ptr<1>, f32
    llvm.store %next0, %out0 : f32, !llvm.ptr<1>
    %out1 = llvm.getelementptr %output[%c1] : (!llvm.ptr<1>, i32) -> !llvm.ptr<1>, f32
    llvm.store %next1, %out1 : f32, !llvm.ptr<1>
    llvm.return
  }
}
```

Run with a build containing this change:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess

from triton import knobs
from triton._C.libtriton import ir, llvm
from triton.backends.compiler import GPUTarget
from triton.backends.nvidia.compiler import CUDABackend, get_features

llvm.init_targets()
backend = CUDABackend(GPUTarget("cuda", 100, 32))
options = backend.parse_options({})
for enabled in (False, True):
    name = "custom" if enabled else "generic"
    context = ir.context()
    ir.load_dialects(context)
    module = ir.parse_mlir_module("example.mlir", context)
    llvm_context = llvm.context()
    llmod = llvm.to_module(module, llvm_context)
    next(iter(llmod.get_functions())).set_calling_conv(71)  # PTX_Kernel
    llvm.attach_datalayout(llmod, "nvptx64-nvidia-cuda", "sm_100a",
                           get_features(options, 100))
    llvm.optimize_module(llmod, llvm.OPTIMIZE_O3,
                         disable_slp_vectorizer=True,
                         nvptx_compute_capability=100,
                         enable_nvptx_tti=enabled)
    Path(f"{name}.ll").write_text(str(llmod))
    metadata = {}
    ptx = backend.make_ptx(str(llmod), metadata, options, 100)
    Path(f"{name}.ptx").write_text(ptx)
    cubin_path = Path(f"{name}.cubin")
    cubin_path.write_bytes(backend.make_cubin(ptx, metadata, options, 100))
    sass = subprocess.check_output(
        [knobs.nvidia.nvdisasm.path, "-c", str(cubin_path)], text=True)
    Path(f"{name}.sass").write_text(sass)
    del llmod, llvm_context, module, context
```

</details>

commits.comment: 该 commit 修复 CDNA5 上多重 cluster barrier 场景的挂起：CDNA5 的 cluster barrier 由单比特 'Cluster Barrier Wave State' 实现，当快 warp 连续通过两次 cluster arrive 而慢 warp 尚未到达第一次 cluster wait 时，慢 warp 通过第一次 cluster barrier 会消耗完成位，但由于快 warp 已越过第二次 arrive，完成位不会再被置位，慢 warp 卡在第二次 cluster barrier。该问题也存在于内核中连续多次使用 cluster 级 atomic（内部会插入 cluster barrier）的情形。按照 CDNA5 指南 5.6.6 的建议，在 TargetInfo::clusterBarrier 中先调用 barrier(loc, rewriter, triton::gpu::AddrSpace::None) 插入 workgroup barrier，再发出 ClusterBarrierArriveOp/ClusterBarrierWaitOp，使同一 workgroup 内各 wave 在每次 cluster barrier 前先同步到齐。测试在 test/Conversion/amd/cluster_barrier_to_llvm.mlir 的 atomic_cluster_barrier 用例中新增一条 CHECK: rocdl.s.barrier{{$}}，验证 atomic 路径产生的 cluster barrier 前确实插入了 workgroup barrier（并保留原有 CHECK-NOT 语义约束）。风险较低：改动局限在 AMD TargetInfo 的 clusterBarrier，可能带来少量额外 barrier 开销（每次 cluster barrier 多一条 s_barrier），但相较挂起是正确的取舍；由于 ascending 不使用 TargetInfoBase/TritonGPUToLLVM（走 TritonToLinalg），不影响其他后端。
commits.message:
[AMD] Always insert a workgroup barrier before cluster barrier (#12342)

Currently the compiler does not follow this recommendation as suggested
in the CDNA5 guide 5.6.6:

> It is recommended that waves in a workgroup first synchronize by using
the workgroup barrier, then one wave per workgroup signals the cluster
barrier.

This will cause some troubles, in this minimal case:

```python
# assume a kernel with 2 cta, 8 warp
gl.amd.cdna5.cluster.arrive() # signal  1
gl.amd.cdna5.cluster.wait()   # barrier 1
gl.amd.cdna5.cluster.arrive() # signal  2
gl.amd.cdna5.cluster.wait()   # barrier 2
```

When 2 warp-0 from 2 ctas reached **signal 2** but a slower warp-n has
not yet reached **barrier 1** (n != 0), the warp-n will pass **barrier
1**, but hang at **barrier 2**. As stated in the guide, cluster barrier
is implemented using "Cluster Barrier Wave State", which has a single
bit to indicate that the cluster barrier has completed. So when the
warp-n reaches **barrier 1**, its cluster-completion bit will be
consumed and there is no other wave-0 to set it again given they have
already passed **signal 2**.

The hang can happen in different variants:
1) When the kernel manually uses more than one cluster barrier
2) When the kernel uses more than one consecutive atomics, which under
the hood will insert cluster barriers

A kernel-side remedy is to always insert a barrier before cluster
barrier / atomics. This PR proposes to directly insert it when lowering
the cluster barrier.
